```{r}
# ==============================================================================
# FIGURE 4 — FINAL FOUR-PANEL VERSION
#
# A: Top 17 largest represented 5′ LTR families — expression heatmap
# B: 5′ LTR family RL000019 — Control / Cold / Heat TE profiles
# C: Data-driven heterogeneous 5′ LTR family — all five conditions, gray lines
# D: k = 17 expression-cluster heatmap — readable condition/replicate labels
#
# Panel A and the RL000019 analysis are retained from the original Figure 4.
# ==============================================================================



# ==============================================================================
# FIGURE 4 — FINAL STANDALONE SCRIPT
#
# Reproduces the THREE plots shown on Slide 4 of the rough-draft PowerPoint:
#
#   A. Individual-TE expression heatmap grouped by 5′ LTR SiLiX family
#   B. All variable expressed structural-TE heatmap
#   C. RL000019 individual-TE Control/Cold/Heat expression profiles
#
# This script is completely independent and can be run from a clean R session.
# ==============================================================================


# ==============================================================================
# 1. PACKAGES
# ==============================================================================

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(tibble)
library(readr)
library(ggplot2)
library(pheatmap)
library(matrixStats)
library(scales)
library(patchwork)
library(gtable)
library(grid)


# ==============================================================================
# 2. PATHS
# ==============================================================================

scratch_dir <- paste0(
  "/projects/standard/hirschc1/menar060/",
  "stress_scratch_copy/stress_scratch"
)

counts_path <- file.path(
  scratch_dir,
  "raw_counts_structural_LTRs_only.txt"
)

metadata_path <- file.path(
  scratch_dir,
  "metadata.csv"
)

fiveprime_silix_path <- paste0(
  "/projects/standard/hirschc1/menar060/",
  "family_analysis/redo_five_prime/B73/output/",
  "B73_five_prime_silix.out"
)

output_dir <- "/users/2/menar060/final_panel_figures"

dir.create(
  output_dir,
  recursive = TRUE,
  showWarnings = FALSE
)


# ==============================================================================
# 3. COLORS
# ==============================================================================

divergent_palette <- c(
  "#27408B",
  "#1B9E77",
  "#2AA198",
  "#56B4E9",
  "#E6AB02",
  "#D55E6A",
  "#984EA3",
  "#7F1D3A"
)

condition_colors <- c(
  "control" = "#777777",
  "heat" = divergent_palette[8],
  "cold" = divergent_palette[4],
  "salt" = divergent_palette[2],
  "UV" = divergent_palette[5]
)

heatmap_colors <- grDevices::colorRampPalette(
  c(
    divergent_palette[1],
    "white",
    divergent_palette[8]
  )
)(101)


# ==============================================================================
# 4. READ METADATA
# ==============================================================================

metadata <- read.csv(
  metadata_path,
  check.names = FALSE
)

if ("SampleID" %in% names(metadata)) {
  rownames(metadata) <- metadata$SampleID
} else {
  rownames(metadata) <- metadata[[1]]
}

if (!"Condition" %in% names(metadata)) {
  stop("metadata.csv must contain a Condition column.")
}

metadata$Condition <- as.character(
  metadata$Condition
)


# ==============================================================================
# 5. READ STRUCTURAL-TE FEATURECOUNTS MATRIX
# ==============================================================================

raw_counts <- readr::read_tsv(
  counts_path,
  comment = "#",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

if (!"Geneid" %in% names(raw_counts)) {
  stop("Geneid column not found in count matrix.")
}

annotation_columns <- c(
  "Geneid",
  "Chr",
  "Start",
  "End",
  "Strand",
  "Length"
)

sample_columns <- setdiff(
  names(raw_counts),
  annotation_columns
)

count_df <- raw_counts %>%
  dplyr::select(
    Geneid,
    dplyr::all_of(sample_columns)
  ) %>%
  as.data.frame()

rownames(count_df) <- count_df$Geneid
count_df$Geneid <- NULL


# ==============================================================================
# 6. CLEAN SAMPLE NAMES
# ==============================================================================

clean_sample_name <- function(x) {

  x <- basename(x)

  x <- sub(
    "_Aligned.*$",
    "",
    x
  )

  x <- sub(
    "\\.bam$",
    "",
    x
  )

  x
}

colnames(count_df) <- clean_sample_name(
  colnames(count_df)
)

count_df[] <- lapply(
  count_df,
  as.numeric
)


# ==============================================================================
# 7. MATCH COUNTS TO METADATA
# ==============================================================================

common_samples <- intersect(
  colnames(count_df),
  rownames(metadata)
)

if (length(common_samples) < 2) {
  stop("Fewer than two samples matched between counts and metadata.")
}

count_df <- count_df[
  ,
  common_samples,
  drop = FALSE
]

metadata <- metadata[
  common_samples,
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

stopifnot(
  identical(
    colnames(count_df),
    rownames(metadata)
  )
)


# ==============================================================================
# 8. EXPRESSION FILTER
#
# Same analysis used for the Slide-4 heatmaps:
#   >1 assigned read equivalent in at least 2 samples
# ==============================================================================

count_matrix <- as.matrix(
  count_df
)

storage.mode(count_matrix) <- "numeric"

minimum_count <- 1
minimum_samples <- 2

keep_expressed <- rowSums(
  count_matrix > minimum_count
) >= minimum_samples

count_matrix_filtered <- count_matrix[
  keep_expressed,
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]


# ==============================================================================
# 9. CPM + LOG2(CPM + 1)
# ==============================================================================

library_sizes <- colSums(
  count_matrix_filtered
)

cpm_matrix <- sweep(
  count_matrix_filtered,
  2,
  library_sizes,
  "/"
) * 1000000

log_cpm_matrix <- log2(
  cpm_matrix + 1
)


# ==============================================================================
# 10. REMOVE ZERO-VARIANCE TES
# ==============================================================================

te_variance <- matrixStats::rowVars(
  log_cpm_matrix
)

keep_variable <- is.finite(
  te_variance
) &
  te_variance > 0

log_cpm_variable <- log_cpm_matrix[
  keep_variable,
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]


# ==============================================================================
# 11. SCALE EXPRESSION WITHIN EACH TE
# ==============================================================================

scaled_expression <- t(
  scale(
    t(
      log_cpm_variable
    )
  )
)

valid_scaled_rows <- apply(
  scaled_expression,
  1,
  function(x) {
    all(
      is.finite(x)
    )
  }
)

scaled_expression <- scaled_expression[
  valid_scaled_rows,
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]


# ==============================================================================
# 12. SAMPLE ANNOTATION
# ==============================================================================

sample_annotation <- data.frame(
  Condition =
    metadata[
      colnames(scaled_expression),
      "Condition"
    ]
)

rownames(sample_annotation) <- colnames(
  scaled_expression
)

annotation_colors <- list(
  Condition =
    condition_colors[
      intersect(
        names(condition_colors),
        unique(
          as.character(
            sample_annotation$Condition
          )
        )
      )
    ]
)


# ==============================================================================
# 13. HUMAN-READABLE SAMPLE LABELS
# ==============================================================================

sample_label_map <- c(
  "SRR1238715" = "Heat rep 1",
  "SRR1819196" = "Heat rep 2",
  "SRR1819198" = "Heat rep 3",

  "SRR1238717" = "Cold rep 1",
  "SRR1819204" = "Cold rep 2",
  "SRR1819205" = "Cold rep 3",

  "SRR1238718" = "Control rep 1",
  "SRR1819617" = "Control rep 2",
  "SRR1819621" = "Control rep 3",

  "SRR1238719" = "Salt",
  "SRR1238720" = "UV"
)

missing_sample_labels <- setdiff(
  colnames(scaled_expression),
  names(sample_label_map)
)

if (length(missing_sample_labels) > 0) {
  stop(
    "The following samples are missing labels: ",
    paste(
      missing_sample_labels,
      collapse = ", "
    )
  )
}

scaled_expression_labeled <- scaled_expression

colnames(
  scaled_expression_labeled
) <- unname(
  sample_label_map[
    colnames(scaled_expression)
  ]
)

sample_annotation_labeled <- sample_annotation

rownames(
  sample_annotation_labeled
) <- unname(
  sample_label_map[
    rownames(sample_annotation)
  ]
)

sample_annotation_labeled <- sample_annotation_labeled[
  colnames(scaled_expression_labeled),
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]


# ==============================================================================
# 14. HELPER HEATMAP — PRESERVE PANEL A COLUMN CLUSTERING
#
# This is NOT a displayed panel.
#
# The original Figure 4 Panel A borrowed the sample/column dendrogram from the
# all-variable-TE heatmap. We retain that exact helper analysis here so Panel A
# is not changed when the displayed heatmap is moved to Panel D.
# ==============================================================================

all_te_heatmap_result <- pheatmap::pheatmap(
  scaled_expression_labeled,

  cluster_rows = TRUE,
  cluster_cols = TRUE,
  clustering_method = "average",

  show_rownames = FALSE,
  show_colnames = FALSE,

  annotation_col =
    sample_annotation_labeled,

  annotation_colors =
    annotation_colors,

  color =
    heatmap_colors,

  breaks =
    seq(
      -3,
      3,
      length.out = 102
    ),

  border_color = NA,
  main = "",
  silent = TRUE
)


# ==============================================================================
# 15. READ 5′ LTR SILIX FAMILY ASSIGNMENTS
# ==============================================================================

silix_raw <- readr::read_tsv(
  fiveprime_silix_path,
  col_names = c(
    "Five_Prime_Family_ID",
    "Attributes"
  ),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

fiveprime_family_assignments <- silix_raw %>%
  dplyr::mutate(

    lLTR_ID =
      sub(
        "^ID=([^;]+);.*$",
        "\\1",
        Attributes
      ),

    # Exact final conversion used in the original analysis:
    # lLTR_51885 -> LTRRT_51885
    TE_ID =
      sub(
        "^lLTR_",
        "LTRRT_",
        lLTR_ID
      )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    Five_Prime_Family_ID,
    lLTR_ID,
    TE_ID
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    !is.na(Five_Prime_Family_ID),
    !is.na(TE_ID)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::distinct(
    TE_ID,
    .keep_all = TRUE
  )


# ==============================================================================
# 16. MATCH EXPRESSION TES TO 5′ LTR FAMILIES
# ==============================================================================

expression_te_map <- tibble::tibble(
  TE_ID =
    rownames(
      scaled_expression_labeled
    )
)

fiveprime_expression_membership <- expression_te_map %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    fiveprime_family_assignments %>%
      dplyr::select(
        TE_ID,
        Five_Prime_Family_ID
      ),
    by = "TE_ID"
  )

fiveprime_expression_matched <- fiveprime_expression_membership %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    !is.na(
      Five_Prime_Family_ID
    )
  )

cat(
  "\n============================================================\n",
  "5′ LTR FAMILY MATCH SUMMARY\n",
  "============================================================\n",
  "Expression TEs: ",
  scales::comma(
    nrow(
      fiveprime_expression_membership
    )
  ),
  "\nMatched to 5′ LTR family: ",
  scales::comma(
    nrow(
      fiveprime_expression_matched
    )
  ),
  "\n5′ LTR families represented: ",
  scales::comma(
    dplyr::n_distinct(
      fiveprime_expression_matched$Five_Prime_Family_ID
    )
  ),
  "\n",
  sep = ""
)


# ==============================================================================
# 17. COUNT EXPRESSED TES PER 5′ LTR FAMILY
# ==============================================================================

fiveprime_family_sizes_expression <- fiveprime_expression_matched %>%
  dplyr::count(
    Five_Prime_Family_ID,
    name = "Number_Expressed_TEs"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(
    dplyr::desc(
      Number_Expressed_TEs
    ),
    Five_Prime_Family_ID
  )

fiveprime_family_order <-
  fiveprime_family_sizes_expression$Five_Prime_Family_ID


# ==============================================================================
# 18. ORDER TES WITHIN EACH FAMILY BY EXPRESSION PROFILE
# ==============================================================================

ordered_te_ids <- character(0)
family_end_positions <- integer(0)
running_total <- 0

for (fam in fiveprime_family_order) {

  family_te_ids <- fiveprime_expression_matched %>%
    dplyr::filter(
      Five_Prime_Family_ID == fam
    ) %>%
    dplyr::pull(
      TE_ID
    )

  family_matrix <- scaled_expression_labeled[
    family_te_ids,
    ,
    drop = FALSE
  ]

  if (nrow(family_matrix) > 1) {

    family_distance <- stats::dist(
      family_matrix
    )

    family_hclust <- stats::hclust(
      family_distance,
      method = "average"
    )

    family_te_ids <-
      rownames(
        family_matrix
      )[
        family_hclust$order
      ]
  }

  ordered_te_ids <- c(
    ordered_te_ids,
    family_te_ids
  )

  running_total <-
    running_total +
    length(
      family_te_ids
    )

  family_end_positions <- c(
    family_end_positions,
    running_total
  )
}

family_end_positions <- head(
  family_end_positions,
  -1
)

fiveprime_family_ordered_expression <-
  scaled_expression_labeled[
    ordered_te_ids,
    ,
    drop = FALSE
  ]


# ==============================================================================
# 19. FAMILY-SIZE ROW ANNOTATION
# ==============================================================================

fiveprime_row_annotation <- fiveprime_expression_matched %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    fiveprime_family_sizes_expression,
    by = "Five_Prime_Family_ID"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(

    Family_Size_Class =
      dplyr::case_when(

        Number_Expressed_TEs == 1 ~
          "Singleton",

        Number_Expressed_TEs >= 2 &
          Number_Expressed_TEs <= 5 ~
          "2–5 TEs",

        Number_Expressed_TEs >= 6 &
          Number_Expressed_TEs < 20 ~
          "6–19 TEs",

        Number_Expressed_TEs >= 20 ~
          "≥20 TEs"
      )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    TE_ID,
    Family_Size_Class
  ) %>%
  tibble::column_to_rownames(
    "TE_ID"
  )

fiveprime_row_annotation <-
  fiveprime_row_annotation[
    ordered_te_ids,
    ,
    drop = FALSE
  ]

fiveprime_annotation_colors <- list(

  Condition =
    condition_colors,

  Family_Size_Class = c(
    "Singleton" = "#D9D9D9",
    "2–5 TEs" = divergent_palette[3],
    "6–19 TEs" = divergent_palette[5],
    "≥20 TEs" = divergent_palette[7]
  )
)


# ==============================================================================
# 20. PANEL-A SUBSET — TOP 17 LARGEST 5′ LTR FAMILIES
#
# "Largest" is defined by the number of expressed TEs represented in the
# expression dataset used for Figure 4.
# ==============================================================================

panel_a_family_ids <- fiveprime_family_sizes_expression %>%
  dplyr::arrange(
    dplyr::desc(Number_Expressed_TEs),
    Five_Prime_Family_ID
  ) %>%
  dplyr::slice_head(
    n = 17
  ) %>%
  dplyr::pull(
    Five_Prime_Family_ID
  )

panel_a_te_ids <- fiveprime_expression_matched %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    Five_Prime_Family_ID %in% panel_a_family_ids
  ) %>%
  dplyr::pull(
    TE_ID
  )

# Preserve the family ordering and within-family hierarchical TE ordering
# established above.
panel_a_ordered_te_ids <- ordered_te_ids[
  ordered_te_ids %in% panel_a_te_ids
]

panel_a_expression <- scaled_expression_labeled[
  panel_a_ordered_te_ids,
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

panel_a_row_annotation <- fiveprime_row_annotation[
  panel_a_ordered_te_ids,
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

# Preserve the existing heatmap family order, but restrict it to the selected
# top 17 families.
panel_a_family_order <- fiveprime_family_order[
  fiveprime_family_order %in% panel_a_family_ids
]

# Recalculate visible gaps so each of the 17 families remains visually distinct.
panel_a_gap_positions <- integer(0)
running_total <- 0

for (fam in panel_a_family_order) {

  family_n <- fiveprime_family_sizes_expression %>%
    dplyr::filter(
      Five_Prime_Family_ID == fam
    ) %>%
    dplyr::pull(
      Number_Expressed_TEs
    )

  running_total <- running_total + family_n

  if (
    fam != tail(
      panel_a_family_order,
      1
    )
  ) {
    panel_a_gap_positions <- c(
      panel_a_gap_positions,
      running_total
    )
  }
}

cat(
  "\n============================================================\n",
  "PANEL A FAMILY FILTER\n",
  "============================================================\n",
  "Top 17 largest 5′ LTR families by number of expressed TEs\n",
  "Families retained: ",
  length(panel_a_family_ids),
  "\nTEs retained in Panel A: ",
  scales::comma(nrow(panel_a_expression)),
  "\n\nSelected families:\n",
  sep = ""
)

print(
  fiveprime_family_sizes_expression %>%
    dplyr::filter(
      Five_Prime_Family_ID %in% panel_a_family_ids
    ) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(
      dplyr::desc(Number_Expressed_TEs),
      Five_Prime_Family_ID
    )
)


# ==============================================================================
# 21. PANEL A — TOP 17 LARGEST 5′ LTR FAMILIES
#
# Panel A uses the EXACT SAME CONDITION/SAMPLE COLUMN CLUSTERING as Panel B.
# We pass Panel B's column hclust object directly to pheatmap, so the column
# dendrogram and sample order are identical between the two heatmaps.
# ==============================================================================

if (is.null(all_te_heatmap_result$tree_col)) {
  stop("Panel B did not return a column clustering tree.")
}

family_heatmap_result <- pheatmap::pheatmap(
  panel_a_expression,

  cluster_rows = FALSE,

  # Reuse Panel B's column tree rather than independently clustering Panel A.
  cluster_cols = all_te_heatmap_result$tree_col,

  show_rownames = FALSE,
  show_colnames = TRUE,

  annotation_col =
    sample_annotation_labeled,

  annotation_colors =
    list(
      Condition = condition_colors
    ),

  gaps_row =
    panel_a_gap_positions,

  color =
    heatmap_colors,

  breaks =
    seq(
      -3,
      3,
      length.out = 102
    ),

  border_color = NA,

  fontsize_col = 9,

  angle_col = 45,

  main = "",

  silent = TRUE
)

# Add extra blank space to the LEFT of Panel A so the first rotated sample
# label ("Heat rep 1") is not clipped by the heatmap boundary.
panel_a_gtable <- family_heatmap_result$gtable

panel_a_gtable <- gtable::gtable_add_cols(
  panel_a_gtable,
  grid::unit(0.35, "in"),
  pos = 0
)

panel_a <- patchwork::wrap_elements(
  full = panel_a_gtable
)


# ==============================================================================
# 22. BUILD DATA FOR RL000019 LINE GRAPH
# ==============================================================================

all_family_expression <- scaled_expression_labeled[
  fiveprime_expression_matched$TE_ID,
  ,
  drop = FALSE
] %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column(
    "TE_ID"
  ) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = -TE_ID,
    names_to = "Sample",
    values_to = "Scaled_Expression"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    fiveprime_expression_matched %>%
      dplyr::select(
        TE_ID,
        Five_Prime_Family_ID
      ),
    by = "TE_ID"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(

    Condition =
      dplyr::case_when(

        grepl(
          "^Control",
          Sample,
          ignore.case = TRUE
        ) ~ "Control",

        grepl(
          "^Heat",
          Sample,
          ignore.case = TRUE
        ) ~ "Heat",

        grepl(
          "^Cold",
          Sample,
          ignore.case = TRUE
        ) ~ "Cold",

        grepl(
          "^Salt",
          Sample,
          ignore.case = TRUE
        ) ~ "Salt",

        grepl(
          "^UV",
          Sample,
          ignore.case = TRUE
        ) ~ "UV",

        TRUE ~ NA_character_
      )
  )


# ==============================================================================
# 23. CLASSIFY HEAT-HIGH / COLD-HIGH TES
#
# Same threshold as the original Slide-4 analysis:
#   Heat - Cold >=  0.5  -> Heat-high
#   Heat - Cold <= -0.5  -> Cold-high
# ==============================================================================

all_te_heat_cold <- all_family_expression %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    Condition %in%
      c(
        "Heat",
        "Cold"
      )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(
    Five_Prime_Family_ID,
    TE_ID,
    Condition
  ) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    Mean_Expression =
      mean(
        Scaled_Expression,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = Condition,
    values_from = Mean_Expression
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    !is.na(Heat),
    !is.na(Cold)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(

    Heat_minus_Cold =
      Heat - Cold,

    Expression_Pattern =
      dplyr::case_when(

        Heat_minus_Cold >= 0.5 ~
          "Heat-high",

        Heat_minus_Cold <= -0.5 ~
          "Cold-high",

        TRUE ~
          "No strong preference"
      )
  )


# ==============================================================================
# 24. PANEL B — RL000019 CONTROL / COLD / HEAT PROFILE
#
# This is the LINE GRAPH on Slide 4.
# ==============================================================================

family_to_plot <- "RL000019"

family_pattern_table <- all_te_heat_cold %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    Five_Prime_Family_ID == family_to_plot
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    TE_ID,
    Expression_Pattern,
    Heat_minus_Cold
  )

family_condition_expression <- all_family_expression %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    Five_Prime_Family_ID == family_to_plot
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    !is.na(Condition)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(
    TE_ID,
    Condition
  ) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    Mean_Scaled_Expression =
      mean(
        Scaled_Expression,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

family_plot_data <- family_condition_expression %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    family_pattern_table,
    by = "TE_ID"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    Condition %in%
      c(
        "Control",
        "Cold",
        "Heat"
      )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(

    Condition =
      factor(
        Condition,
        levels = c(
          "Control",
          "Cold",
          "Heat"
        )
      ),

    Expression_Pattern =
      factor(
        Expression_Pattern,
        levels = c(
          "No strong preference",
          "Cold-high",
          "Heat-high"
        )
      )
  )

neutral_data <- family_plot_data %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    Expression_Pattern ==
      "No strong preference"
  )

responsive_data <- family_plot_data %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    Expression_Pattern %in%
      c(
        "Cold-high",
        "Heat-high"
      )
  )

profile_colors <- c(
  "Heat-high" = "#D55E6A",
  "Cold-high" = "#27408B",
  "No strong preference" = "#BDBDBD"
)

panel_b <- ggplot2::ggplot() +

  ggplot2::geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed",
    linewidth = 0.45,
    color = "grey55"
  ) +

  ggplot2::geom_line(
    data = neutral_data,
    ggplot2::aes(
      x = Condition,
      y = Mean_Scaled_Expression,
      group = TE_ID
    ),
    color =
      profile_colors[
        "No strong preference"
      ],
    linewidth = 0.45,
    alpha = 0.30
  ) +

  ggplot2::geom_line(
    data = responsive_data,
    ggplot2::aes(
      x = Condition,
      y = Mean_Scaled_Expression,
      group = TE_ID,
      color = Expression_Pattern
    ),
    linewidth = 0.8,
    alpha = 0.65
  ) +

  ggplot2::geom_point(
    data = responsive_data,
    ggplot2::aes(
      x = Condition,
      y = Mean_Scaled_Expression,
      color = Expression_Pattern
    ),
    size = 1.8,
    alpha = 0.75
  ) +

  ggplot2::scale_color_manual(
    values = profile_colors,
    breaks = c(
      "Heat-high",
      "Cold-high"
    ),
    labels = c(
      "Heat-high",
      "Cold-high"
    )
  ) +

  ggplot2::labs(
    x = "Condition",
    y = "Mean scaled expression",
    color = "Expression pattern",
    title = paste0("5′ LTR family ", family_to_plot)
  ) +

  ggplot2::theme_classic(
    base_size = 12
  ) +

  ggplot2::theme(

    plot.title =
      ggplot2::element_text(
        face = "bold",
        size = 12,
        hjust = 0.5
      ),

    axis.title =
      ggplot2::element_text(
        face = "bold"
      ),

    axis.text.x =
      ggplot2::element_text(
        face = "bold",
        size = 11
      ),

    axis.text.y =
      ggplot2::element_text(
        size = 10
      ),

    legend.position =
      "top",

    legend.title =
      ggplot2::element_text(
        face = "bold"
      )
  )


# ==============================================================================
# 25. RECREATE THE FINAL k = 17 EXPRESSION-CLUSTER SOLUTION
#
# This uses the same final settings as the original large analysis:
#   set.seed(123)
#   nstart = 100
#   iter.max = 300
# ==============================================================================

set.seed(123)

km17 <- stats::kmeans(
  scaled_expression,
  centers = 17,
  nstart = 100,
  iter.max = 300
)

te_expression_clusters <- tibble::tibble(
  TE_ID = rownames(scaled_expression),

  Expression_Cluster = factor(
    km17$cluster,
    levels = 1:17
  )
)


# ==============================================================================
# 26. PANEL C — DATA-DRIVEN EXAMPLE OF WITHIN-FAMILY EXPRESSION HETEROGENEITY
#
# Goal:
#   Select a sequence-defined 5′ LTR family whose individual TEs have strongly
#   different expression profiles across control, cold, heat, salt, and UV.
#
# Selection is DATA-DRIVEN rather than hard-coded:
#   1. Require >=10 expressed TEs in the family.
#   2. Calculate each TE's mean scaled expression in each condition.
#   3. Keep families represented in all five conditions.
#   4. For each family, calculate all pairwise Euclidean distances among the
#      five-condition TE expression profiles.
#   5. Choose the family with the largest median pairwise profile distance.
#
# Thus Panel C is explicitly an example of a 5′ LTR sequence family whose
# members show highly heterogeneous stress-response profiles.
# ==============================================================================

condition_order_panel_c <- c(
  "Control",
  "Cold",
  "Heat",
  "Salt",
  "UV"
)

# Mean scaled expression for each TE in each condition.
all_family_condition_expression <- all_family_expression %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    !is.na(Condition)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(
    Five_Prime_Family_ID,
    TE_ID,
    Condition
  ) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    Mean_Scaled_Expression =
      mean(
        Scaled_Expression,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Family sizes in the expression dataset.
candidate_family_sizes <- all_family_condition_expression %>%
  dplyr::distinct(
    Five_Prime_Family_ID,
    TE_ID
  ) %>%
  dplyr::count(
    Five_Prime_Family_ID,
    name = "Number_Expressed_TEs"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    Number_Expressed_TEs >= 10
  )

# Build one five-condition expression vector per TE.
candidate_profile_wide <- all_family_condition_expression %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    Five_Prime_Family_ID %in%
      candidate_family_sizes$Five_Prime_Family_ID
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    Condition %in% condition_order_panel_c
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Condition =
      factor(
        Condition,
        levels = condition_order_panel_c
      )
  ) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = Condition,
    values_from = Mean_Scaled_Expression
  )

# Score each candidate family by median pairwise distance among TE profiles.
candidate_family_ids <- unique(
  candidate_profile_wide$Five_Prime_Family_ID
)

family_heterogeneity_scores <- lapply(
  candidate_family_ids,
  function(fam) {

    fam_df <- candidate_profile_wide %>%
      dplyr::filter(
        Five_Prime_Family_ID == fam
      )

    profile_matrix <- fam_df %>%
      dplyr::select(
        dplyr::all_of(
          condition_order_panel_c
        )
      ) %>%
      as.matrix()

    # Require complete profiles for this example panel.
    complete_rows <- stats::complete.cases(
      profile_matrix
    )

    profile_matrix <- profile_matrix[
      complete_rows,
      ,
      drop = FALSE
    ]

    if (nrow(profile_matrix) < 10) {
      return(
        tibble::tibble(
          Five_Prime_Family_ID = fam,
          Number_Complete_TEs = nrow(profile_matrix),
          Median_Profile_Distance = NA_real_,
          Maximum_Profile_Distance = NA_real_
        )
      )
    }

    pairwise_distances <- as.numeric(
      stats::dist(
        profile_matrix,
        method = "euclidean"
      )
    )

    tibble::tibble(
      Five_Prime_Family_ID = fam,
      Number_Complete_TEs = nrow(profile_matrix),
      Median_Profile_Distance =
        stats::median(
          pairwise_distances,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),
      Maximum_Profile_Distance =
        max(
          pairwise_distances,
          na.rm = TRUE
        )
    )
  }
) %>%
  dplyr::bind_rows() %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    is.finite(Median_Profile_Distance)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(
    dplyr::desc(Median_Profile_Distance),
    dplyr::desc(Maximum_Profile_Distance),
    dplyr::desc(Number_Complete_TEs),
    Five_Prime_Family_ID
  )

if (nrow(family_heterogeneity_scores) == 0) {
  stop(
    "No 5′ LTR family with >=10 TEs had complete profiles across all five conditions."
  )
}

heterogeneous_family_to_plot <-
  family_heterogeneity_scores$Five_Prime_Family_ID[1]

cat(
  "\n============================================================\n",
  "PANEL C — HETEROGENEOUS 5′ LTR FAMILY\n",
  "============================================================\n",
  "Selected family: ",
  heterogeneous_family_to_plot,
  "\nComplete TEs: ",
  family_heterogeneity_scores$Number_Complete_TEs[1],
  "\nMedian pairwise profile distance: ",
  round(
    family_heterogeneity_scores$Median_Profile_Distance[1],
    3
  ),
  "\nMaximum pairwise profile distance: ",
  round(
    family_heterogeneity_scores$Maximum_Profile_Distance[1],
    3
  ),
  "\n",
  sep = ""
)

# Save the complete family ranking so the selected example is transparent.
readr::write_tsv(
  family_heterogeneity_scores,
  file.path(
    output_dir,
    "5prime_family_all_stress_expression_heterogeneity_ranking.tsv"
  )
)

# Prepare Panel C data.
panel_c_data <- all_family_condition_expression %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    Five_Prime_Family_ID ==
      heterogeneous_family_to_plot
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    Condition %in%
      condition_order_panel_c
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Condition =
      factor(
        Condition,
        levels =
          condition_order_panel_c
      )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    te_expression_clusters,
    by = "TE_ID"
  )

# Plot all individual TE profiles in a single neutral color.
# The purpose of this panel is to show the range of expression behavior within
# one sequence-defined 5′ LTR family, not the k=17 cluster assignments.

panel_c <- ggplot2::ggplot(
  panel_c_data,
  ggplot2::aes(
    x = Condition,
    y = Mean_Scaled_Expression,
    group = TE_ID
  )
) +

  ggplot2::geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed",
    linewidth = 0.45,
    color = "grey55"
  ) +

  ggplot2::geom_line(
    color = "grey45",
    linewidth = 0.7,
    alpha = 0.65
  ) +

  ggplot2::geom_point(
    color = "grey45",
    size = 1.6,
    alpha = 0.75
  ) +

  ggplot2::labs(
    x = "Condition",
    y = "Mean scaled expression",
    title =
      paste0(
        "5′ LTR family ",
        heterogeneous_family_to_plot
      )
  ) +

  ggplot2::theme_classic(
    base_size = 12
  ) +

  ggplot2::theme(
    plot.title =
      ggplot2::element_text(
        face = "bold",
        size = 12,
        hjust = 0.5
      ),

    axis.title =
      ggplot2::element_text(
        face = "bold"
      ),

    axis.text.x =
      ggplot2::element_text(
        face = "bold",
        size = 10
      ),

    axis.text.y =
      ggplot2::element_text(
        size = 10
      ),

    legend.position = "none"
  )


# 27. PANEL D — k = 17 STRUCTURAL TE EXPRESSION-CLUSTER HEATMAP
#
# This reproduces the expression-cluster heatmap from the original large
# analysis, with one requested presentation change:
#
#   show_colnames = FALSE
#
# Therefore SRR/sample labels are not printed beneath the heatmap.
# ==============================================================================

shared_te_ids_d <- intersect(
  rownames(scaled_expression_labeled),
  te_expression_clusters$TE_ID
)

panel_d_matrix <- scaled_expression_labeled[
  shared_te_ids_d,
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

panel_d_cluster_vector <-
  te_expression_clusters$Expression_Cluster[
    match(
      rownames(panel_d_matrix),
      te_expression_clusters$TE_ID
    )
  ]

# Order rows by expression cluster, exactly as in the original heatmap.
panel_d_row_order <- order(
  as.integer(
    panel_d_cluster_vector
  )
)

panel_d_matrix <- panel_d_matrix[
  panel_d_row_order,
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

panel_d_cluster_vector <-
  panel_d_cluster_vector[
    panel_d_row_order
  ]

panel_d_row_annotation <- data.frame(
  Expression_Cluster =
    panel_d_cluster_vector
)

rownames(
  panel_d_row_annotation
) <- rownames(
  panel_d_matrix
)

panel_d_sample_annotation <-
  sample_annotation_labeled[
    colnames(panel_d_matrix),
    ,
    drop = FALSE
  ]

# Use the exact condition-color definitions from the original k=17 heatmap.
panel_d_condition_colors <- c(
  "control" = "grey60",
  "heat" = divergent_palette[8],
  "cold" = divergent_palette[4],
  "salt" = divergent_palette[5],
  "UV" = divergent_palette[7]
)

panel_d_cluster_colors <- grDevices::hcl.colors(
  17,
  palette = "Dynamic"
)

names(
  panel_d_cluster_colors
) <- as.character(
  1:17
)

panel_d_annotation_colors <- list(
  Condition =
    panel_d_condition_colors,

  Expression_Cluster =
    panel_d_cluster_colors
)

panel_d_cluster_sizes <- table(
  panel_d_cluster_vector
)

panel_d_gaps_row <- cumsum(
  panel_d_cluster_sizes
)

panel_d_gaps_row <-
  panel_d_gaps_row[
    -length(
      panel_d_gaps_row
    )
  ]

expression_cluster_heatmap_result <- pheatmap::pheatmap(
  panel_d_matrix,

  cluster_rows = FALSE,

  cluster_cols = TRUE,

  annotation_row =
    panel_d_row_annotation,

  annotation_col =
    panel_d_sample_annotation,

  annotation_colors =
    panel_d_annotation_colors,

  gaps_row =
    panel_d_gaps_row,

  color =
    heatmap_colors,

  breaks =
    seq(
      -3,
      3,
      length.out = 102
    ),

  show_rownames = FALSE,

  # Show condition/replicate labels beneath Panel D, matching Panel A.
  show_colnames = TRUE,

  border_color = NA,

  fontsize_col = 9,

  angle_col = 45,

  annotation_names_row = FALSE,

  annotation_names_col = FALSE,

  main = "",

  silent = TRUE
)

panel_d <- patchwork::wrap_elements(
  full =
    expression_cluster_heatmap_result$gtable
)


# ==============================================================================
# 28. DISPLAY / SAVE INDIVIDUAL PANELS
# ==============================================================================

print(
  family_heatmap_result
)

print(
  panel_b
)

print(
  panel_c
)

print(
  expression_cluster_heatmap_result
)


# Preserve the original RL000019 panel as a standalone output.
ggplot2::ggsave(
  filename = file.path(
    output_dir,
    "RL000019_Control_Cold_Heat_expression_profiles.jpeg"
  ),
  plot = panel_b,
  width = 7,
  height = 5,
  units = "in",
  dpi = 600,
  bg = "white"
)

ggplot2::ggsave(
  filename = file.path(
    output_dir,
    "RL000019_Control_Cold_Heat_expression_profiles.pdf"
  ),
  plot = panel_b,
  width = 7,
  height = 5,
  units = "in",
  bg = "white"
)


# Save the newly selected heterogeneous-family example.
ggplot2::ggsave(
  filename = file.path(
    output_dir,
    paste0(
      heterogeneous_family_to_plot,
      "_all_stress_expression_profiles.jpeg"
    )
  ),
  plot = panel_c,
  width = 7,
  height = 5,
  units = "in",
  dpi = 600,
  bg = "white"
)

ggplot2::ggsave(
  filename = file.path(
    output_dir,
    paste0(
      heterogeneous_family_to_plot,
      "_all_stress_expression_profiles.pdf"
    )
  ),
  plot = panel_c,
  width = 7,
  height = 5,
  units = "in",
  bg = "white"
)


# ==============================================================================
# 29. COMBINE THE FOUR FIGURE-4 PANELS
#
# Layout:
#
#   A = top 17 largest 5′ LTR family heatmap
#   B = original RL000019 Control/Cold/Heat line graph
#   C = data-driven heterogeneous 5′ LTR family line graph across all stresses
#   D = k=17 expression-cluster heatmap with sample labels hidden
#
# A and D are given more vertical space because they are heatmaps.
# ==============================================================================

figure4_final <- (
  panel_a |
  panel_b
) /
(
  panel_c |
  panel_d
) +

  patchwork::plot_layout(
    heights = c(
      1,
      1
    ),
    widths = c(
      1.28,
      1
    )
  ) +

  patchwork::plot_annotation(
    tag_levels = "A"
  ) &

  ggplot2::theme(
    # Retain the enlarged tag styling previously used to match Figures 1–3.
    plot.tag =
      ggplot2::element_text(
        face = "bold",
        size = 23
      ),

    plot.tag.position =
      c(
        0.01,
        0.99
      )
  )

print(
  figure4_final
)


ggplot2::ggsave(
  filename = file.path(
    output_dir,
    "Figure4_FINAL.jpeg"
  ),
  plot = figure4_final,
  width = 15,
  height = 15,
  units = "in",
  dpi = 600,
  bg = "white"
)


ggplot2::ggsave(
  filename = file.path(
    output_dir,
    "Figure4_FINAL.pdf"
  ),
  plot = figure4_final,
  width = 15,
  height = 15,
  units = "in",
  bg = "white"
)


# ==============================================================================
# 30. FINAL CHECKS
# ==============================================================================

cat(
  "\n============================================================\n",
  "FIGURE 4 COMPLETE\n",
  "============================================================\n",

  "Panel A: top 17 largest 5′ LTR family heatmap\n",
  "Panel B: original RL000019 Control/Cold/Heat profiles\n",
  "Panel C: heterogeneous 5′ LTR family across Control/Cold/Heat/Salt/UV; neutral TE profiles\n",
  "Panel D: k=17 expression-cluster heatmap; condition/replicate labels shown\n\n",

  "Variable expressed TEs: ",
  scales::comma(
    nrow(
      scaled_expression
    )
  ),

  "\nMatched to 5′ LTR families: ",
  scales::comma(
    nrow(
      fiveprime_expression_matched
    )
  ),

  "\nRL000019 TEs plotted in Panel B: ",
  scales::comma(
    dplyr::n_distinct(
      family_plot_data$TE_ID
    )
  ),

  "\nPanel C selected family: ",
  heterogeneous_family_to_plot,

  "\nPanel C TEs plotted: ",
  scales::comma(
    dplyr::n_distinct(
      panel_c_data$TE_ID
    )
  ),

  "\n\nOutputs:\n",
  file.path(
    output_dir,
    "Figure4_FINAL.jpeg"
  ),
  "\n",
  file.path(
    output_dir,
    "Figure4_FINAL.pdf"
  ),
  "\n",

  sep = ""
)
```
